title: Pope needs no further treatment for lung cancer, his doctors say
summary: Pope Leo will not ‌need any further therapy after undergoing ​lung cancer surgery ​last week, his doctors said in ​a statement released by ‌the Vatican on Wednesday.

image.caption: Pope Leo arrives to hold his first weekly general audience in St. Peter's Square since cancer surgery, at the Vatican, Wednesday. His doctors released a statement saying the Pope will not require further therapy for lung cancer. (Yara Nardi/Reuters)

blocks.text: Pope Leo will not ‌need any further therapy after undergoing ​lung cancer surgery ​last week, his doctors said in ​a statement released by ‌the Vatican on Wednesday.
Pope Leo was diagnosed with pulmonary adenocarcinoma after part of his lung was removed
Pope Leo will not ‌need any further therapy after undergoing ​lung cancer surgery ​last week, his doctors said in ​a statement ⁠released ⁠by ‌the Vatican on Wednesday.
Histological examination results confirmed a ⁠diagnosis of pulmonary adenocarcinoma, a common form of lung cancer, with the disease ‌remaining localized, the doctors said.
"A subsequent oncological evaluation ​has confirmed ⁠that no further therapy ⁠is required," the ⁠Pope's ⁠lead ​surgeon, Stefano Margaritora, and ​his ⁠personal physician, Luigi Carbone, said.

The Pope returned to St. Peter's Square Wednesday, waving to pilgrims and blessing babies from his open-air Popemobile as he held his first general audience at the Vatican since undergoing surgery Oct. 13.
After touring the Square, Leo offered a sermon in Italian. In the only major change from previous occasions, he gave brief greetings afterwards in seven other languages, instead of nine.

The 71-year-old is due to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from Nov. 6 to 17, in one of the most intense trips arranged for a Catholic leader in decades, but it remains unclear if that trip will go ahead as planned.
His lead surgeon has indicated he believes Leo will be well enough to travel.
"I would say there are no clinical reasons why this visit should not take place," he said in an interview with Vatican News.
